### Historical audit: S0087

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 5 is available.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Line 7, student `model_request`, chars [0,243171) | The explicit goal was to reconstruct an indoor photograph as editable meshes with matching camera, framing and materials. The first program modeled multiple separate assets: paneled room, parquet, chaise, pillow, card, foreground chair and curtains. Those labels and estimated anchors express the student’s interpretation, not independent verification of the photograph. |
| Line 7, same event | The program grouped chaise parts and parented upholstery panels to the chaise; this shows intended hierarchy, not verified physical contact. It rotated the pillow and foreground chair, used procedural fabric and wood materials, and specified camera, world and area lights. Whether their pose, connections, textures, lighting and framing matched the reference cannot be checked from the supplied text alone. |
| Line 7, embedded step 1 result | The runner reported `ok: true` and `usable_render: true`, with a saved render. The student was supplied image paths for the reference and render; the images themselves are not visible in this audit. This is execution/render success, not geometric or visual correctness. |
| Line 8, student `codex_session`, chars [0,3484); line 9, student `model_response`, chars [0,14918) | A fresh, read-only review session completed with zero tool calls. The student’s own review described the chaise as too small and rightward, wall slopes as excessive, and floor/upholstery as washed out. These are reported diagnoses, not independently confirmed observations. |
| Lines 9–10, student response and `execute` step 2, chars [0,14918) and [0,15634) | The revision changed camera position and roll while retaining the 48 lens, darkened the floor, reduced lighting, changed textile patterns, widened the seat, enlarged/rotated the pillow and moved the foreground chair. The revised complete program was submitted for execution. No step 2 result is visible here. |

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher input, detection, diagnosis, proposed update or adoption is visible in this chunk. The student’s render review and revision are autonomous within the supplied procedure; the record does not establish additional exploration or receipt of unseen advice.

**Outcome and lessons.** Step 1 has formal runner-reported success; final task outcome and step 2 correctness are **unknown**, not an established algorithm failure, empty patch or interruption. A transferable observation is that a runnable render and a scene hierarchy do not validate visual similarity or part contact. The particular camera, lighting and furniture adjustments are task-specific hypotheses. Unresolved: whether step 2 ran successfully, whether its changes improved the image, and whether object connections, occlusions and materials actually matched the reference.
